focus.note: A phrasal verb is a verb plus a small word. The small word often changes the meaning completely, so learn them together.

speak.title: Role-play: the book or the film first?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: You want your friend to read the novel before you both see the film. Explain why the book is worth the time. Listen, then agree on a plan.

b.text: You want to see the film this weekend, before people tell you the story. Explain why. Listen, then agree on a plan.

phrases: I'd rather read the book first.
That's a fair point, but it's a long book.
What if we watched it and then read it?
I don't want anyone to spoil the ending.
I'm not sure the film can explain all the science.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class what you decided and why.
